Zelenskyy rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality and said he refused to cede territory to Russia.
US negotiators have floated the idea that Ukraine should cede parts of eastern Donbas in exchange for NATO membership, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, after the latest rounds ⁠of Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi and Ireland.
This is the first time the question of linking NATO membership to territorial concessions has been raised, Zelenskyy told reporters in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
“The Americans raised a question: ‘What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from ⁠Donbas?” he said. “That is why I believe NATO is back on the agenda.”
Zelenskyy said the parts of the Donbas region in eastern Ukraine the US asked about were areas Russia does not control. The Ukrainian president said he refused to cede territory.
“[Russian President Vladimir] Putin’s desire to change borders in Europe is a fact. I am sure this is part of his concept of revising security guarantees in Europe,” he said. “This is dangerous because, in my view, it is precisely things like this that lead to wars or escalations.”
Putin has long said that Ukrainian membership of NATO is a red line for Moscow, citing the issue as one reason for launching Russia’s full-blown invasion in 2022.
Zelenskyy did say that if Ukraine received a comprehensive package, including security guarantees, military and reconstruction funds, and a recovery plan from the US and other partners, he would put the question about ceding parts of Donbas to a national referendum.
“If the American side confirms precisely this to us, together with other NATO partners, then I will ask our Ukrainian society what it thinks: do we accept it or not?” Zelenskyy said.
He stressed that any arrangement would not involve recognising occupied territories as Russian. Zelenskyy also rejected the possibility of Ukraine committing to neutrality, saying that would require changing the country’s constitution.
“If Putin expects Ukraine’s neutrality to be enshrined, that’s not going to happen,” he said. “We’re not in NATO right now anyway.”
Despite the diplomatic push to end the conflict, Russia and Ukraine reported numerous overnight attacks . Russian officials reported on Friday that about 1,200 Ukrainian drones were fired at the country, with oil infrastructure among the targets, while Ukraine reported attacks on a hospital and the port of Odesa.
At the summit in Ireland over recent days, EU leaders agreed that Europe’s team for any Ukraine peace talks would comprise five major military powers – non-EU member Britain plus France, Germany, Italy and Poland – as well as EU officials. They would hold talks ‌with ‌US and Ukrainian officials, but not with Russia.
texts.https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cwvg:
US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said.
The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, which come after US President Donald Trump's envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable.
Russia controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory.
Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
"The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday.
He went on to say that if he received a specific proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum.
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow.
Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted. It has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal.
Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion.
It is not clear the US is actually proposing Nato membership – the White House has not yet replied to a request for comment and it is understood that Ukraine itself sees that as unrealistic.
Other Nato members are wary and the Kremlin has always been fiercely opposed. It is one reason why Russia started this war in the first place.
It is possible the American envoys were exploring Ukraine's "red lines" when it comes to occupied land in the Donbas. Zelensky said recently that the US mediators believed Kyiv only had to cede territory to achieve peace and were applying pressure, keen to do a deal as soon as possible.
Ukraine is sure that Russia's ambitions are far greater and has long seen Nato as its only sure protection.
So it is also possible that Zelensky made this suggestion public in order to re-open a discussion that had been considered all-but closed.
He maintains that the idea is now "back on the agenda" as part of an "extremely difficult conversation" on European security.
It also looks like Ukrainian push-back against Russia's renewed hardline stance. Moscow now talks about a "new European security architecture", which is long-standing Russian code for a weaker Nato.
The issue appears to have been the main focus at the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week.
Russia has insisted again that it will not agree to cease fighting until a final peace deal is in place that would include handing over territories its troops have not captured, in addition to the Crimean peninsula it annexed illegally in 2014.
Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas.
The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices.
Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service , which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" and called for fresh elections.
Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership.

Radiation and collisions reshape the planetary building materials.
Beta Pictoris is a young star, roughly 20 million years old, and located about 64 light-years away from Earth. It is surrounded by a vast disk of dust and rubble where planets are still forming—astronomers have already found three. In a new Science study, a team led by Sarah Betti, an astronomer at the Space Telescope Science Institute in Baltimore, used the James Webb Space Telescope to look for ice in this disk. Researchers found both water and carbon dioxide ice.
The water ice is glassy rather than crystalline, and it is mixed with carbon dioxide in roughly the same proportions we see in comets of our own Solar System. This suggests ingredients necessary to form water-rich worlds might be common around young stars.
Beta Pictoris is one of the best studied stars in the sky. Its disk was among the first ever imaged, back in 1984, and we see it almost exactly edge-on, which makes it a natural laboratory for studying how planetary systems grow. It’s what astronomers call a debris disk, where the dust is constantly replenished by collisions among comets and planetesimals, small bodies that are the building blocks of planets.
The outer parts of the disk are far enough from the star that water and other volatile molecules should freeze into solid ice. The disk holds a large reservoir of carbon monoxide gas, which ultraviolet light from the star should destroy within 50 to 300 years. For that gas to still be there, something must keep replenishing it—most likely it’s released from ice when volatile-rich comets collide. The properties of the planet Beta Pictoris b also suggest it formed from ice-rich material.
Yet despite plenty of reasons to suspect the system is full of ice, earlier searches have failed to find it. Attempts to detect water vapor found nothing, and a search for the telltale dip that water ice leaves in starlight at a wavelength of 3 micrometers also failed.
According to theoretical models, ultraviolet radiation from the star can destroy small grains of pure ice faster than collisions can produce them. On the other hand, grains of dirty ice, mixed with other molecules, should survive longer.
Betti and her colleagues observed Beta Pictoris on December 7, 2023, using Webb’s Near Infrared Spectrograph (NIRSpec). They operated it in a mode that records a full spectrum, from 0.6 to 5.2 micrometers, for every point in the image. After subtracting the overwhelming glare of the star, the team measured how much starlight the disk’s dust reflects at each wavelength to look for the fingerprints of ices.
Water ice absorbs light strongly near 3 micrometers, while carbon dioxide ice absorbs either at 4.27 micrometers or 4.39 micrometers when it contains the heavier carbon-13 isotope. The team first mapped the water ice features across the disk and found they were strikingly uniform. They then extracted detailed spectra from two spots on opposite sides of the star, each roughly 100 astronomical units out.
Both spectra showed water and carbon dioxide ices, the latter in both its common form and the rarer carbon-13 version. But the shape of those features turned out to tell us more than the fact they were there.
The carbon dioxide features were shifted slightly toward shorter wavelengths and were much broader than those of pure carbon dioxide ice measured in the lab. The team says in the paper that this is how carbon dioxide behaves when its molecules are trapped inside water ice. In other words, the two ices aren’t sitting side by side as separate grains—they are thoroughly mixed, which makes it the kind of dirty ice that models suggested could survive the star’s ultraviolet radiation.
The team calculated that there is slightly more than one carbon dioxide molecule for every 10 water molecules, meaning it’s about 11 percent of the ice. That falls within the 2.5 to 30 percent range measured in Solar System comets and the 7 to 20 percent seen in the ice of disks around other newborn stars. It means the ices of Beta Pictoris may have formed through the same processes as in our own Solar System, building up on dust grains in cold, dense, water-rich clouds during the earliest stages of star formation.
The structure of the water ice also pointed in this direction. When water freezes at moderate temperatures, its molecules settle into an orderly crystal lattice, and crystalline ice produces a sharp peak in the spectrum just above 3 micrometers. That peak was absent at Beta Pictoris. The ice is almost entirely amorphous, a disordered, glass-like solid that forms when water molecules freeze so fast and so cold that they stick wherever they land. The team estimates that less than 7 percent of the water ice in the system is crystalline, which is somewhat surprising.
Models predicted that ice in debris disks should mostly be crystalline. For amorphous ice to stay in that form, it has to remain colder than about 100 Kelvin, or minus 173° Celsius. Otherwise, something has to keep breaking up its crystal structure, such as high-energy ultraviolet light, cosmic rays, or particles streaming from the star. Either way, the researchers concluded the ice most likely formed in the interstellar medium, long before the planets of Beta Pictoris began to take shape.
The remaining question was how the icy grains got spread so evenly across the disk.
The team argues that this even ice distribution requires frequent collisions among planetesimals. Each collision would release fresh icy dust, including ice that had been buried and protected deep inside the colliding bodies, replenishing what the starlight destroys. We already have evidence that such collisions do happen. Earlier infrared images revealed a curved, lopsided streak of dust in the southwestern arm of the disk, thought to be debris from a violent collision a little less than halfway out from the star.
Betti’s team’s findings support the idea that the disk’s carbon monoxide gas comes from colliding icy bodies and offer an explanation of how ice can survive in an environment constantly exposed to ultraviolet light. What the team could not do is determine exactly how much crystalline ice is present or rule out other molecules hiding in the mixture.
But if a young planetary system 64 light-years away may have started with much the same icy ingredients as ours, then primordial, interstellar ice might be a common ingredient of planetary systems in general. This means the raw materials for water-rich, potentially habitable worlds might be common, too.

Philippines' Carmelle has won the first Eurovision Song Contest Asia with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra
The Philippines have won the very first Eurovision Song Contest Asia, hosted in Bangkok and with 11 countries vying for the title.
Nineteen-year-old singer Carmelle was always a front runner with her women's empowerment anthem Sobra-Sobra, complete with its catchy rap section.
She earned 211 points in total - 93 from the jury and 118 from the public vote - ahead of Thailand's MANG x DAOU in second place with 170 points.
There was a joyous atmosphere at the One Bangkok Arena as the crowd cheered the contestants and celebrated the popular winner.
Carmelle was the youngest contestant in the comeptions at 19 years old
Carmelle, the youngest contestant in the competition, was an obvious favourite with the juries and the public despite strong showings from several nations.
Other notable acts included MANG x DAOU, whose emotive duet Aroma elicited huge cheers from the home crowd.
Bangladeshi beatboxers Beatmosphere eschewed the traditional backing track, instead using their voices to replicate the sounds of drums and basslines.
And Laos's Thinla performed her crowd-pleasing song Bae in a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit.
However, the Laotian song had a unintentional second outing after the music video was played over an apparent technical issue during the broadcast - meaning it was the last song the audience heard before the vote.
Thinla wore a traditional Lao hilltribe outfit during her performance
The voting system worked much the same as the European Eurovison, with the public vote accounting for 50% of the result and the other 50% coming from the 11 national juries - with additional points awarded from a rest of the world vote.
Also performing during the broadcast was 2026 Eurovision Song Contest winner Dara from Bulgaria, who performed her winning song Bangaranga and new song Bad Idea.
Thai superstar Jeff Satur also made an appearance, hitting the high notes in his performance of Black Tie.
Eurovision in Asia was an idea that has been talked about for decades, but one that never seemed to materialise - despite many false starts - until now.
There is a huge enthusiasm here for Eurovision Asia, but a large number of the audience were established fans of the original contest from other countries and regions of the world.
Speaking after the show, fan Zelie Pereira - who travelled from Scotland to Thailand to attend - said she was "very happy" with Carmelle's win.
Eurvosion superfans Michael, Scarlett and Zelie travelled from the UK to Thailand to watch Eurovision Asia's first outing
Korea, Vietnam and Laos also received praise from Pereira and her friends Michael Peters and Scarlett Massie, both from England.
"The dance was amazing. The sets were amazing. The costumes were amazing. The singing was amazing. Incredible", Peters added.
They confidently declared that "Asia Vision" should be the name for next year's show.
For some, it seems the excitement for another edition is already building.
However the crowd at the One Bangkok Arena thinned out not long after the Philippines singer Carmelle lifted the trophy.
The arena was crowded, but not full, and it's still not clear how much commitment there is among regional broadcasters to keep the contest going and expand it to more than 11 countries.

Filipino entry, pop and rap song Sobra-Sobra, takes 19-year-old to victory at grand final in Bangkok
Carmelle Collado has won the first Eurovision song contest Asia, taking the Philippines’ entry, Sobra-Sobra , to victory in Bangkok on Saturday night, at the first regional edition of the contest to be staged outside Europe.
Eleven countries competed at the One Bangkok Forum in central Bangkok, and the show ran for two and a half hours including advertising.
The winner, who performs under the single name Carmelle, finished on 211 points, 41 clear of the hosts Thailand , with Vietnam third. She received the most votes from both the national juries and the public ballot.
Carmelle, 19, grew up beside the railway tracks in the Bicol region of south-eastern Luzon and has been competing in televised talent contests since she was 12.
Sobra-Sobra mixes pop and rap, is supported by traditional Philippine instruments, the kubing and kulintang, and is sung in Tagalog and English.
After her victory, Carmelle said her song celebrated female empowerment and was intended as “a tribute to all Filipino women”.
“I made history, since this was the first time,” she told the Associated Press. “It’s such a big responsibility for me, because this one is a global stage, so thank you everybody who voted for me.”
“It’s about how unapologetic, independent and strong Filipinas are,” she told the Guardian before the final. “It describes me – not just me, but of course all the Filipinas.”
The show opened with a routine celebrating the host country, in which Muay Thai fighters shared the stage with drag performers on street food carts. The 11 acts were then driven on in tuk-tuks, each carrying their national flag.
Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên , a star at home for more than 20 years, performed first, among dancers costumed as lotus leaves. Mang x Daou represented Thailand, a duo assembled for the contest in the host country who performed a duet staged like a musical number.
Nepal’s Pratik Himal Rai gave one of the most conventionally Eurovision performances of the night with Ananta Maya , a rock ballad staged with fire imagery and a large heart-shaped structure behind him.
He ended it by appealing for support for his country, which he said was “going [through a] very hard situation”. More than 1,500 people were killed and more than 5,000 were reported missing after a rock and ice avalanche near the Chinese border triggered catastrophic flash floods in August.
Bangladesh’s Beatmosphere , originally a nine-member a cappella and beatbox group, sang without a single instrument. Three of their members were left out of the final due to a rule capping each act at six performers on stage.
Nyendra from Bhutan sang dressed in the gho, his country’s national dress for men, against a backdrop of Himalayan peaks. Mongolia’s Beck performed in a reinterpreted deel, also a national costume.
Half the result was decided before the show began. The 11 national juries voted at a dress rehearsal on Friday night and put the Philippines at the top with 93 points, ahead of Vietnam and Malaysia.
The other half came from viewers around the world, who could vote online but not for their own country, and who were given eight free votes each and the option to buy 10 more.
Laos’s entrant, Thinla, was unable to hear her own music during her performance, and her dress rehearsal was aired once all live performances were over. She finished fifth, with the night’s third-highest public score.
Carmelle receives no prize money but does get a trophy presented by Dara, the Bulgarian singer who won this year’s European contest , and will perform at Eurovision 2027 in Burgas.
Organisers have said the right to stage future editions will not automatically go to the winner, on the grounds that smaller countries lack the infrastructure.
Some of the clearest echoes of Eurovision’s camp traditions came through those who announced the votes.
South Korea’s jury points were read by Jo Kwon, a veteran pop star who has played Adam in the Korean production of Priscilla, Queen of the Desert and the title role in Everybody’s Talking About Jamie.
The Philippines’ were read by Vice Ganda, a gay comedian who is one of the biggest stars on Philippine television.
Meanwhile, the guest performer was the Thai singer Jeff Satur, who reached a wider Asian audience through KinnPorsche, a 2022 series in the genre of male same-sex romance dramas that has a large following across Asia.
Organisers intend the Bangkok show to be the first of many regional editions, with the executive producer, Assaf Blecher, saying that 16 or 17 territories had expressed interest in competing next year, among them China, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

Prime ministerial hopeful calls Arab minority ‘an integral part of the Israeli story’ as he seeks to form government
Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot condemned a “racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation” against the country’s Arab citizens, after the caretaker prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, accused Arab parties of electoral fraud without evidence.
Netanyahu has repeatedly targeted Arab parties and Palestinian citizens of Israel after his party received a disappointing electoral showing, accusing them of manipulating the election and being linked to Hamas. Israeli electoral authorities have rejected these claims as not being backed by evidence.
Arab citizens of Israel, the vast majority of them of Palestinian descent, comprise more than 20% of the country’s population.
Shin Bet, Israel’s internal security branch, sought to question four Arab lawmakers, including the Arab-majority Ra’am party head, Mansour Abbas, leading to accusations that the security agency had become politicised.
“Arab citizens of Israel are an integral part of the Israeli story. The attempt to marginalise them and vilify them collectively is a profound violation of the principles of statesmanship,” Eisenkot said in a statement on Friday.
Eisenkot’s statement was a rare instance of a prominent Jewish political leader taking a strong stand in defence of Arab Israelis.
The statement also reflected political realities in Israel, as Arab parties found themselves kingmakers after the latest election. The two Arab-majority parties, Ra’am and the Joint List, secured 19 seats in the October election.
They have the potential to help Eisenkot form a governing coalition and become Israel’s next prime minister. If Eisenkot cannot form a coalition within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension, the mandate to form a government would pass to another lawmaker, potentially Netanyahu.
Eisenkot has to balance the competing interests of several parties if he hopes to form a coalition. Rightwing elements of the opposition have pledged to drop their support of the prospective PM if he cooperates with Arab parties.
His statement on Friday portrayed a more statesman-like approach to ruling than his more rightwing, demagogic opponents who have used Arab parties and citizens as political scapegoats over the last three years.
“[Arab citizens] have been subjected to a racist and aggressive campaign of delegitimisation, fuelled by the outgoing prime minister and those around him for political purposes,” Eisenkot said in his statement.
“The prime minister of Israel is the prime minister of all Israeli citizens, including those who did not vote for him,” he added.
Netanyahu and his allies have repeatedly criticised leaders of Arab parties for refusing to describe Hamas as a “terror group” after its unprecedented 7 October 2023 attack on Israel.
All leaders of Arab parties have condemned the attack, in which Arab Israelis – descendants of Palestinians who remained in what became Israel in 1948 – were also among those killed.
In a speech, Netanyahu falsely claimed that the two Arab lists sought to establish either an “Islamic state” or a “nationalist Palestinian state”.
During the same ceremony, the national security minister, Itamar Ben Gvir, heckled Joint List’s leader, Yousef Jabareen, during his oath of allegiance, accusing him of having “pledged allegiance to Hamas”.
“It is entirely legitimate to disagree with representatives of the Arab parties, even to strongly disapprove of some of them. But it is neither legitimate nor acceptable to malign an entire community, and I will not allow it,” Eisenkot said.
President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with forming a new government on Sunday after consultations in which a majority of political parties, including the two Arab lists, recommended him for the role.
Israeli media has reported that Eisenkot has also been reaching out to the country’s ultra-Orthodox parties for a potential alliance. The issue of the ultra-Orthodox not serving in the Israeli military was one of the hot button issues during the October election, with Eisenkot previously saying they should also be included in the country’s mandatory draft.

Healthy soils, native plants, and fewer chemicals are helping vineyards adapt.
More than 500 vineyards are scattered across the slopes and valleys of South Africa’s Western Cape , one of the world’s most biologically diverse landscapes. The region produces about 90 percent of South Africa’s wine , but winemakers there are increasingly struggling with drought, excessive heat and erratic rainfall.
Temperatures in the region have risen 1.5 to 2 times faster than the global average over the past five decades. And extreme storms have become more intense as climate variability increases. The late 2010s brought a significant challenge for winemakers, as three years of severe drought placed vineyards under intense stress and reduced grape production.
As climate variability places increasing pressure on grape production, many wine producers are building on sustainability measures that have long been part of vineyard management.
We are a team of geographers and sustainability scientists who study environmental change , environmental health, conservation, agriculture and land management. Our team wanted to better understand how farmers in South Africa’s wine-producing regions are responding as a range of environmental and economic pressures rise. We talked with growers, conservation practitioners and wine industry experts in the Western Cape and analyzed how 107 vineyards , about 20% of the total, were using sustainable land stewardship practices to adapt.
In many agricultural landscapes, production and conservation goals are frequently viewed as competing priorities . But our research found that many vineyard operators in the Western Cape see long-term stewardship and conservation of soil and wildlife habitat as essential strategies for business success.
The Western Cape is home to the Cape Floral Region , a global biodiversity hot spot. It includes fynbos , a unique biome containing thousands of endemic plant species, including types of proteas , ericas and restios that are found nowhere else on Earth.
Sustainability certification and conservation programs, such as World Wildlife Fund Conservation Champions , have helped encourage vineyards to protect biodiversity in the region. Many growers use these sustainability certifications to increase their wine’s marketability. But we found they have also embraced conservation for how it can benefit their vineyards. Rather than viewing conservation as land taken out of production, many said they see it supporting the ecological processes essential to their business.
The majority of South Africa’s vineyards today participate in the Integrated Production of Wine certification system, created by the South African wine industry and researchers in 1998 to reduce environmental harm. The system sets standards governing pesticide use, water management, wastewater treatment and environmental stewardship. It also uses independent auditing of participating farms and wineries to ensure those claiming certification meet the standards.
To manage the water supplies their vineyards depend on, growers described restoring native vegetation , including the removal of alien species, along waterways and reducing erosion to protect wetlands and rivers. Research shows that healthy natural systems can improve water retention in the soil and contribute to the overall resilience of the landscape in the face of more extreme climate conditions.
To boost their soil’s health, some growers are planting cover crops , such as legumes , cereals like oats and rye, and brassicas such as radish and mustard, between vine rows. Growers broadly described using cover crops, compost, mulching and other practices to improve soil structure and increase organic matter in the soil. Cover crops require maintenance and can provide habitat for pests, but research shows that the right cover crops, when well maintained, can benefit vineyards by reducing erosion and increasing water retention and nutrients in the soil.
Several producers also described efforts to reduce their reliance on chemical pesticides, which is beneficial not only for the environment but also their businesses as chemical costs continue to rise . We heard about vineyards that monitor pest populations closely and respond in targeted ways rather than using pesticides broadly.
Some growers encourage beneficial insects and manage habitats that support natural pest control . The creation of habitats for natural pest predators can reduce the overall disease risk too. While chemical treatments remain part of many vineyard operations, growers reported increasing interest in other approaches that prevent disease and pest outbreaks, such as pruning, to reduce their total chemical use.
Sustainable practices like these are well established in South Africa’s wine industry, but our interviews suggest their use has been expanding in recent years. Rather than focusing solely on treating problems after they arise, these approaches emphasize prevention, monitoring and ecological balance.
The stewardship practices we observed in South Africa are investments in long-term business resilience for many growers.
Many of the wine producers we interviewed described facing rising costs and market uncertainty. Exports, labor and chemicals are all expensive. They emphasized that maintaining healthy soils, conserving water and reducing vulnerability to drought and disease are essential to keeping their vineyards productive.
As concerns about drought, climate pressures and profitability rise, the area in vineyard production in South Africa has also decreased . Several growers described diversifying their business models and even switching crops to make their businesses more resilient to hotter, drier conditions.
Farmers around the world are confronting the realities of a changing climate . Our research shows that effective solutions can come from recognizing the interconnectedness of nature and production.
The experience of South Africa’s winegrowers shows that farms can be managed more sustainably when they’re seen as part of larger ecological systems.
Students Zoe Van der Walt , Jack Spining and Dryver Finch contributed to this article.
Hannah V. Herrero is Associate Professor of Geography & Sustainability and Director of Sustainability at University of Tennessee ; Erin L. Bunting is Assistant Professor of Geography at Michigan State University ; Jane Southworth is Professor of Geography at University of Florida ; Jason K. Blackburn is Professor of Geography at University of Florida ; and Stephanie Insalaco-Wyner is Assistant Professor of Geographic Information Sciences at Southwestern University .

Israeli caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday renewed his call for a national unity government with Gadi Eisenkot, who dismissed the appeal as a political ploy. This comes as the incoming premier is in the midst of negotiations to form a new administration.
Israel 's caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Saturday reiterated his calls for a national unity government with his opponent Gadi Eisenkot , who in turn dismissed the appeal as a ruse.
The latest exchange comes as Eisenkot is in the midst of negotiations to form a government , after he was tapped for the post of premier on Sunday.
Read more Israel's new parliament to be sworn in as Eisenkot prepares government
A meeting with Eisenkot on Thursday "only strengthened the conviction that it is essential to form a national unity government" to guarantee Israel's security, Netanyahu said in a video statement, adding that such a government could "eliminate the Iranian threat once and for all".
He said this government would be made up of parties that recognise Israel "as a state for the Jewish people".
It would address security challenges, he added, most notably Iran which he claimed would "not hesitate to use nuclear weapons against us".
The outgoing prime minister warned against Eisenkot's plan to form a minority government, presented as a "national emergency government".
Such a plan would see the 48 lawmakers in Eisenkot's bloc vote in favour of his government, against the 46 Netanyahu backers. The 26 other members of parliament, from Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties, could abstain, allowing the government to be approved without an absolute majority in the Knesset , which has 120 seats.
"Instead of trying to form a weak and dangerous government... let's meet in one room, without preconditions, put aside all our disagreements and all the boycotts , and reach agreements for the security and the future of the state," Netanyahu urged.
Minutes later, Eisenkot responded by saying Netanyahu "knows he lost the election", accusing him of playing "tricks" by appealing for a unity government.
"Netanyahu is calling for negotiations while they are already underway; he claims to want unity but... sows division and stokes tensions as if there were no tomorrow," the former army chief said, adding that "these tricks don't work on me".
Eisenkot was tapped on Sunday to form a new government within 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension.
Negotiations are expected to be difficult, especially as Netanyahu has waged a campaign to discredit Arab-Israeli parties, which gained a record number of seats in the election.
Netanyahu's proposed unity government would be made up of key Jewish parties ranging from the centre to the right, while excluding the Arab parties.
Read more Eisenkot pushes October 7 inquiry as Netanyahu targets Arab parties in tense new parliament
Eisenkot has indicated he would be open to forming a government with members of Netanyahu's Likud party, as well as outgoing Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich 's Religious Zionism, provided their commitment to unity is "sincere".
But a unity government with Netanyahu himself remains unlikely, particularly after Eisenkot denounced his "racist" campaign against Arab parties on Friday.
Eisenkot on Saturday reiterated his calls for a "break with the extremists", notably supporters of far-right minister Itamar Ben Gvir, as a condition for any participation in a government under his leadership.
Another point of contention is the election on Tuesday of the speaker of the Knesset, a post currently held by Amir Ohana, a close Netanyahu ally. The opposition has put forward Matan Kahana, a former officer in the Israeli army who was fifth on Gadi Eisenkot's list, to replace him.
"If they ( Likud and its allies) are truly seeking a sincere political partnership, as they claim, they must allow the democratic process to unfold normally... and instruct their members of parliament to support the appointment of Matan Kahana," Eisenkot said.

Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans
Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker.
The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt.
The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".
The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."
New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help".
"We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said.
Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference.
Were you in the area at the time of incident? Get in touch .
There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.
Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side, Moreno said.
Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.
The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.
On Saturday, Moreno said that nine people are still in hospital.
She said that the captain of the ship was injured in the accident but refused medical treatment until he knew all passengers and crew were accounted for.
US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue had been an "incredible job".
Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued.
Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what had occurred.
Still covered in dirt from the boat crash, Joe Knab of Kansas told New Orleans NBC affiliate WDSU that the ship quickly capsized after the collision.
He spent about 20 minutes in the water before being rescued.
"When we first went in we were bobbing underneath the water; it was sinking pretty fast, but we finally got out of there," he said.
Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he had seen the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision.
"It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic."
Holford added that he had seen passengers and crew "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking.
The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website.

In Santa Cruz de Succhabamba, the pope urges people not to respond to injustice with brutality.
Pope Leo XIV has called for an end to the violence gripping Peru, urging people not to respond to injustice with brutality, as he visited communities he once served as bishop.
“We feel threatened by the uncertainty of widespread violence and by the unspeakable suffering that continues to afflict so many of our brothers and sisters, he said, speaking at his former cathedral in Chiclayo.
Peru’s homicide rate has nearly doubled over the past five years, from 5.8 to 10.7 per 100,000 people. Reported extortion cases rose from 2,421 in 2019 to 26,734 in 2025, according to official figures cited by The Associated Press.
Security was a top concern for Peruvians in the last election. Conservative President Keiko Jujimori took office in July after promising to tackle crime. She has since declared states of emergency, including in Lima in August, then in September in prisons holding inmates linked to criminal organisations.
She has also pursued closer ties with Washington, bringing Peru into the ‘Shield of the Americas,’ a US-led regional coalition formed to carry out joint military operations against drug cartels.
Later on Saturday, in the Andean town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba with a population of about 6,000, about 20,000 people came to an outdoor Mass, where Leo also addressed violence in society.
“Selfishness, injustice and evil are not overcome by brutality, but by prayer, patience and perseverance in denouncing what is wrong, by making our pleas with determination and working diligently to bring about the necessary changes,” said the leader of the Roman Catholic church.
He also drew attention to the suffering of rural communities he used to serve, where migration and declining birth rates are emptying villages.
“Let us think, for example, of the suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future for themselves and their families in the great coastal cities,” he said.
Originally from Chicago in the United States and formerly known as Robert Francis Prevost, Leo arrived in Santa Cruz de Succhabamba by helicopter and was welcomed by a local band singing “Pope Leo, welcome home.”
He’d made the journey to the remote area many times before during his time as bishop of Chiclayo from 2015 to 2023, driving himself along winding mountain roads in a pick-up truck.
The pope, who holds both US and Peruvian citizenship, spent about two decades working in Peru as a missionary priest and bishop.

The top United States transportation official has said work being performed on an antiquated telecommunications system could be to blame for a rare, hours-long US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that halted all air traffic inside the country.
At a news conference in Washington, DC, on Saturday, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy spoke about routine maintenance that was performed on Friday to upgrade a router from copper to fibre at a “very remote location”.
Duffy said “contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment” caused the router in question to start flooding other ones in the country’s air traffic control system.
“We had 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,” he told reporters at the Department of Transportation.
When those connection issues caused disruption in radar feeds and communications between air traffic controllers and aeroplanes, Duffy said a ground stop was ordered.
“When we see that, your safety is paramount. We shut down the airspace,” he said.
The Transportation Department identified the contractor of Friday’s maintenance as L3Harris, a US-based aerospace and defence company that has been tasked with modernising the communications system for the FAA.
“What we’re working to determine was whether we had incompetence, meaning was it … installator error from L3Harris? Or did they install a faulty router?” Duffy said. “We haven’t determined what the fault was.”
Duffy added that L3Harris, which he said had performed decades of work for the FAA, “didn’t meet the moment”.
“They own this network. They’re our prime contractor. I can’t go somewhere else. They own it,” he said. “Or was it a faulty router? And we’re going to find that out. And frankly, we’re going to hold people accountable.”
In response to Duffy’s allegations, L3Harris told Al Jazeera it has been working “in close coordination with the FAA” and places safety and reliability as its “highest priorities”.
“We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the November 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel,” a spokesperson for the company said. “L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.”
Amid concerns that Friday’s ground stop was the result of a cyberattack, the US government said Saturday it did not “believe” that was the cause.
“Once we were able to isolate the work being done at this location, all of our systems came back online,” Duffy said. “So, we don’t believe this was cyber at all.”
The head of the FAA, who also spoke at Saturday’s news conference, echoed the transportation secretary’s remarks, saying the system outage was caused by an equipment error.
“We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related,” FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said.
A root cause analysis would be shared with the public when it is available, he added.
As airlines and thousands of travellers begin the process of digging out from Friday’s groundstop, the longest and only second nationwide stop since 9/11, the FAA said full schedule integrity is expected by the end of Sunday.
“We have crews and aircraft that are out of position for 12,000 flights that were lost,” Bedford said. “These crews, pilots and flight attendants need to get to their points of reconnection with their schedules.”
Bedford said the FAA expects about 4,000 to 5,000 flights out of the 41,000 scheduled on Saturday to be cancelled.
“That will set us up for a full recovery tomorrow,” he said. “I do think the worst is behind us.”

The UN climate chief has warned that "tactical delays" at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey could prevent a deal to slow global warming.
The United Nations' top climate official urged negotiators at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey to "avoid tactical delays" that would prevent a deal to stop global warming.
Delegates from more than 200 nations are gathered in the Mediterranean city of Antalya with the core goal of preventing the planet from warming by 2 degrees Celsius (3.6 degrees Fahrenheit).
Downtown, thousands of civil society and environmental activists from around the world protested against the consequences of climate change .
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
Simon Stiell, executive secretary of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), said getting an agreement is "tough but vital work."
"There ​is no collective success without compromise from every party," he added.
"As we head into the second week, ​I urge ‌parties to move swiftly to the hardest issues and to avoid tactical delays."
Meanwhile, tens of thousands of protesters marched through Antalya on Saturday for climate protection and human rights, according to organizers.
Many were dismayed at the lack of progress and how the climate crisis is taking a back seat.
"The pursuit of profit at all costs continues to set the [global] agenda [and] govern the trajectory of our world, so there is a need to push back," environmental activist Zaki Mamdoo from South Africa told DW.
Luisa Nebauer, the main organizer of Germany's Fridays for Future movement, lamented that German Chancellor Friedrich Merz was absent from the conference, along with several other European leaders.
"We won't have a chance to solve any of the crises as long as our planet is destabilizing by the hour," Nebauer told DW. "We must show up!"
Turkish authorities permitted the rally to go ahead, in a country that often bans large public gatherings.
Alongside the march, a parallel "People's Climate Summit" involving hundreds of domestic and international civil society groups takes place in Antalya this weekend.
With inflation, wars, deindustrialization and debt being seen as bigger immediate threats, many governments are watering down their commitments to the clean energy transition, along with the billions required to help developing nations to adapt.
The United ⁠States has snubbed the talks ​for the second year in a row under President Donald Trump, who has called climate change a hoax and promoted continued use of fossil fuels.
Delegates also face pressure from large fossil-fuel-producing nations to avoid setting stricter targets for a faster phaseout of oil and gas.
Climate advocates in Antalya are growing increasingly frustrated by the lack of commitment and delaying tactics preventing an ambitious deal.
COP31 is seeking to unlock finance and investment , reduce the use of so-called super-pollutants and methane and ensure food security.
Host Turkey is, meanwhile, pushing a plan to expand global electrification. Yet, some environmental groups are disappointed the proposal doesn't push increased electricity use from renewable sources.
A UN report last month warned that, within a few years, the world is set to exceed the 1.5 degrees Celsius (2.7 degrees Fahrenheit) of warming.
The figure, set at COP21 in 2015, is the threshold beyond which most scientists believe the world will see increasingly extreme effects of climate change.
A first draft of a deal text is expected to emerge next week, according to Australia's ​COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen.

Several social media accounts claiming to represent the Iranian military show signs of being part of so-called content farms. DW Fact Check looks at how they operate and how users can spot them.
As fears of regional escalation grew after US strikes on Iran, US President Donald Trump claimed the US-Israel war with Iran was " effectively over " on November 9 at a White House briefing . "We're just keeping it the status quo."
Periods of heightened public interest, such as the conflict involving Iran, create fertile ground for so-called content farms . Following Trump's statement, posts on the Iran war surged online again. And a growing network of accounts claiming links to Iran's military has accumulated millions of views.
DW Fact Check examined a number of these accounts and found recurring signs of content farm behavior. Experts who reviewed the accounts DW provided describe them as part of a broader ecosystem of pro-Iran content aggregators that connect across multiple social media platforms.
Content farms are websites or social media accounts, or a network of either, producing large amounts of cheap content in a short time span. They may be driven by economic incentives, but they can also serve as vehicles for political influence campaigns.
The internet watchdog NewsGuard has found 165 false claims about the Iran war that collectively have been watched hundreds of millions of times. Only a few of them originated from Iranian state media.
NewsGuard identified the majority as pushing a pro-Iran agenda, shifting toward AI-generated images, and increasingly claiming that accurate stories from authentic media are AI-generated and false.
An analysis by the London-based Institute for Strategic Dialogue (ISD) identified pro-Iran networks of X accounts which revealed signs of coordination, cross-promotion and engagement tactics while spreading misleading and AI-generated war content. It found no links to state-affiliated actors.
Several accounts identified by DW Fact Check use the Iranian flag as their profile picture and a variation of "Iran Military" in their username. While ownership cannot always be verified, they share recurring characteristics commonly associated with content farms.
Content farms use repetitive and formulaic posting formats, as they are cheaper and easier to produce. Their posts frequently start with the word "BREAKING" and imitate the appearance of news updates on the conflict.
One account , called "Iran Military Media," is linked to a Facebook account that Iranian state media have verified as authentic. It has built a substantial audience across multiple social media platforms, with over 290,000 followers on X, 597,000 on Facebook and 17,200 followers on Instagram.
It posts a handful of times a day, often sharing AI-generated or AI-enhanced videos and frequently adopting the " BREAKING " format. Since late 2025, it has published more than 1,600 posts on X, generating over 150 million views and 3.6 million likes.
"The accounts discussed are a central part of this ecosystem as they distribute the pro-Iranian content, state and non-state allied media at relatively low cost and generate millions of views," said Moustafa Ayad, an expert in online influence operations at the ISD.
Ayad examined 10 similar "Iran Military"-themed accounts during the same period, and their combined reach is even greater. Together, they accounted for 12,588 posts, 353 million views and 6.6 million likes.
This network is replicated on Facebook in numerous languages. According to Ayad, this strategy is part of what the late Ayatollah Ali Khamenei outlined as "soft war."
Ayad said the accounts' reach is amplified when they are paired with other accounts. Only a small share of "Iran Military Media's" 150 million views came from reposted content.
A second account , "Iranian Force," has amassed more than 248,000 followers. It typically posts around 10 times a day, though on some days the volume exceeds 30 posts.
Like "Iran Military Media," it frequently relies on " BREAKING " alerts and AI-generated content . It also includes genuine footage, often framed through a pro-Iran lens.
X lists the account as being based in Pakistan and its profile history shows six username changes. In a break from the Iran-related content, one post suddenly defends a Pakistani TikToker and includes an appeal in Urdu to the government in Pakistan.
Charlene Lin, an analyst for the internet watchdog NewsGuard, told DW it had flagged this account for multiple false narratives. According to Lin, it is also linked to another account that spreads the same false narratives in coordination.
A third account , called the "Iran Army," posts a handful of times a day, including AI-generated videos . Its posts regularly reach tens and at times hundreds of thousands of views.
Like "Iranian Force," it distributes videos from official briefings by the Iranian Armed Forces while also using the "BREAKING" format to drive engagement. One post claiming "the war has officially started" received over 41 million views.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
While these accounts differ in reach and post slightly different content, they share many characteristics. The accounts repeatedly share cheaply produced images, at times coordinated between accounts, and make sensational and unverified claims portraying Iran as militarily powerful or politically influential.
Several accounts in this wider ecosystem have faced restrictions. Since March , a number of prominent "Iran Military"-themed accounts have been suspended on X, including " Iran Military Monitor ," which had close to 2 million followers before its removal.
Earlier this year, Iranian state media issued a statement distancing itself from a range of "Iran Military" accounts circulating on social media, stating that only one account was authentic.
Yet for social media users, distinguishing that account from the others may not be straightforward. The verified account uses the same "Iran Military" branding and a similar profile picture, while also sharing AI-generated content and frequent "BREAKING" updates.
Despite differences in authenticity and affiliation, many of these accounts consistently adopt a pro-Iran framing. They portray Iran as militarily capable, able to retaliate against adversaries and enjoying international support, while rarely highlighting information that contradicts that image.
DW Fact Check found repeated postings of the same content close in time across the accounts and different platforms. The "Iranian Force" and "Iran Military Media" accounts have, for example, posted the same image ( here and here ), with the same caption on the same day, as have accounts in the wider "Iran Military Media" network.
"The pro-Iranian ecosystem online is large, multi-layered and cuts across almost all of the various popular social media platforms and messaging services," said the ISD's Ayad. "[It's] a key component to the Iranian government's ability to withstand challenges to its rule both from within and outside, while generating sympathy and connections with other online communities."

US tech giant Microsoft says it has fixed problems that led to a global outage of its services. The glitch severely disrupted online communications in businesses and governments for more than 24 hours.
The US technology conglomerate Microsoft said on Saturday that a more than 24-hour global outage affecting its Microsoft 365 applications used by businesses and governments across the world has now ended.
"We ​have completed our efforts to address ​the underlying issue of the ⁠incident ​and ​restored service to ​the remaining impacted ‌customers and regions," ​the ⁠company posted on X.
Microsoft applications such as Teams, Outlook and Copilot were all hit by the outage, leading to communications problems in scores of countries.
The company has said it was "not aware" of any outside interference that could have been behind the outage, blaming the problem on server issues.
The disruption was one of the longest in Microsoft's history and the second this year.
To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video
The outage, which began around 1725 UTC on Thursday according to web testing and network diagnostics company ​Ookla, affected government agencies and businesses across much of the world.
It made it impossible to carry out activities such as sending emails and holding online meetings.
Germany was no exception, with a spokesperson for its Federal Ministry for Digital Transformation and Government Modernization saying that while the outage did not have a major impact on federal government functions, it did significantly affect ​German businesses.
Britain's state health service (NHS) was also severely affected, with personnel forced to have recourse to paper records rather than those stored online.
Altogether, there were more than 7.4 million reports of problems worldwide logged by Downdetector, which monitors online outages.
The disruption highlights the widespread and perilous reliance of governments and businesses on a very small number of Big Tech companies.
The problems at Microsoft are so far believed to be unconnected with the major communications outage that has affected US aviation.

Noel Fielding has said he is "appalled" by jokes he made alongside Russell Brand when the pair appeared together on TV and at live shows.
The Great British Bake Off presenter said in a statement to the Sun he was "horrified and deeply disturbed" to learn of Brand's crimes, after the disgraced comedian was jailed for rape and sexual assault.
Footage of Fielding and Brand joking about rape with TV presenter Jonathan Ross on an episode of Channel 4's Big Fat Quiz of the Year in 2007 has resurfaced in the aftermath of Brand's conviction.
Fielding described "some of the jokes" he made as "horrible and inappropriate", and said he had not been in contact with Brand "for many years".
"I was horrified and deeply disturbed to learn of Russell Brand's crimes, which I was completely unaware of until they became public knowledge. My thoughts are with the women whose courage brought him to justice," Fielding said.
"I appeared on TV, radio and live charity shows with him, and whilst we played it up for the cameras and in the media, I considered it a professional relationship, rather than a personal one. I have had no contact with him for many years.
"Looking back at some of the jokes I made alongside him I was appalled. They were horrible and inappropriate, and I very much regret them."
Ross has also released a statement distancing himself from the remarks, saying that his "thoughts are with the many, many women who have bravely come forward."
Among the resurfaced footage is a clip of Brand and Fielding laughing on an episode of The Russell Brand Show, which aired on BBC Radio 2 in 2007. In it, Brand joked about kissing and holding an underage grasshopper.
"How do you even know if it's a child or an adult? You don't even care, do you," Fielding responded.
Brand can be heard replying: "It's a mistake I've made. I've had a lot of problems in the past, because I thought a grasshopper was above age. Before I know it, I'm in it, right, I'm kissing it, I'm holding it. Then it turns around and looks at me with onyx eyes and says: 'I'm 12.'"
Brand and Fielding also performed charity gigs together as The Goth Detectives.
Fielding said he was "appalled" by some of the jokes he had made alongside Brand
Brand was jailed for 10 and a half years for raping a woman and sexually assaulting three others.
Further allegations against him have been made in recent days. More women have made allegations about him in interviews with the Times and a Netflix documentary.
The Times said it could not publish the investigation until the criminal case ended. Brand has denied non-consensual sexual activity.
Police have said Brand is being investigated over rape allegations made by two more women.
The disgraced entertainer is being detained at HMP Wandsworth. BBC News has asked his legal representatives for a response to the latest allegations.
If you are affected by any of the issues in this story, help and support is available at BBC Action Line.

A delegation of 18 Democratic lawmakers arrived at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Saturday to reaffirm the US commitment to tackling global warming following their sweeping midterm election victory.
Fresh from their US midterm election triumph , an emboldened group of Democratic lawmakers descended on the COP31 climate talks shunned by President Donald Trump on Saturday to signal their commitment to tackling global warming.
The 18-strong delegation joined the annual UN conference in Turkey after their party regained control of both chambers of Congress in a landslide victory last week cheered by climate campaigners.
Read more Why the Democrats routed the Republicans in the US midterm elections
"Many of our allies and partners across the world think the United States has not been predictable or dependable. So we have a lot of trust to earn back," Florida Representative Kathy Castor told AFP.
"We have so much work to do. And yes, I hope the United States gets back on track with urgent climate action," she said after the group took photos in front of a large COP31 sign in a sprawling expo centre.
The election has been a topic of discussion at COP31 in Antalya, with hopes that Democrats can restore some clean energy policies and that a pro-climate president can be elected in two years.
"What happened in the US is remarkable, and a much needed shift that we all needed, not only from a climate perspective, but overall," Harjeet Singh, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Treaty Initiative, told AFP.
Since taking office in January 2025, Trump has rolled back some of the clean energy policies of his predecessors, promoted oil drilling, pulled the US out of the Paris Agreement and kept his country out of the UN's climate negotiations.
"It is absolutely shameful that the Trump administration operates this way, that this is an administration that is filled with climate deniers, that is beholden to big oil in the United States," Yassamin Ansari, an Arizona lawmaker, told AFP.
Ansari and other members of the delegation spoke at a panel focused on the midterm elections , attracting a crowd that overflowed outside the "America Is All In" pavilion.
The group reminded COP31 delegates that, while Trump has rejected clean energy, US states and local governments have continued to promote renewables and other pro-climate policies.
A group of US mayors and governors visited COP31 earlier this week, along with former US vice president Al Gore and former US climate envoy and secretary of state John Kerry .
"Despite the setbacks that we're experiencing through this Trump administration, climate action is alive in America," California Congressman Raul Ruiz told the panel.
The president's Republican party was handed a resounding defeat last week in large part due to anger over soaring energy prices and Trump's costly war with Iran .
Democrats have vowed to use their majority in the House and the Senate to launch investigations into the administration's climate policies and propose clean energy legislation.
But Trump still has two years left in office and has vowed to wield his veto power.
"At a time where Americans from all political backgrounds want to see their energy bills reduced, this administration will be very hard pressed to veto legislation that will bring down costs for the American people," Ansari said.

Bonnie Tyler died aged 75 after undergoing emergency intestinal surgery in Portugal earlier this year
Bonnie Tyler sings of "love, light and peace" and remembers "the ones who still live on inside our hearts" on her posthumous Christmas single, which was released on Friday.
The popular Welsh powerhouse singer, born Gaynor Hopkins, died in July aged 75 after undergoing emergency intestinal surgery in Portugal earlier this year.
Fans were able to hear the Total Eclipse of the Heart singer's husky tones one more time on the festive track titled "Love, Light and Peace".
The last song Tyler recorded features sleigh bells and angels and an ad-libbed farewell: "To all, goodnight."
The lyrics about grief and loss take on new meaning following her death.
Tyler sings: "Blessed are the ones who still live on inside our hearts.
The song was written by Chrissie Hammond and Grammy-winner Terry Britten, who played guitar on Tyler's debut album, The World Starts Tonight in 1977.
Nearly 50 years later, he returned as a writer and producer for the last song she recorded.
Tyler had "no big ideas" about recording until she was spotted by a talent scout
Tyler's husband of more than 50 years, Robert Sullivan, previously said she would have wanted fans to hear the music she was working on, and gave his blessing for the song's release .
Tyler was born in a Neath council house where she grew up with a love of music before being discovered by talent scout Roger Bell in a Swansea club.
After finding fame she was dubbed "the female Rod Stewart" for her husky vocals, and launched a career that spanned 50 years .
In August, fans travelled to Swansea to line the streets as a celebration of life service was held for her at Swansea Minster.

Çevre, Şehircilik ve İklim Değişikliği Bakanlığı ile COP31 Türkiye iş birliğinde, “Dünya Ortak Evimiz” üst başlığıyla hayata geçirilen festival; küresel iklim krizine, çevresel felaketlere, kuraklığa ve ekolojik yıkımlara sinemanın gücüyle dikkat çekiyor.
Kurmaca, belgesel ve animasyon olmak üzere 3 kategoride dünyanın dört bir yanından yüzlerce eserin başvurduğu yarışmada jüri değerlendirmesinin ardından finale kalan 10 güçlü yapımı sinemaseverlerle buluşturuyor.
Dünyanın dört bir yanından gelen başvuruların değerlendirildiği yarışmanın ön jüri üyeliğini Mustafa Gürbüz, Ömer Dişbudak ve Merve Kuş Mataracı üstlendi.
Ön değerlendirmeyi geçen finalist filmler ise usta yönetmen Derviş Zaim'in başkanlığında; oyuncular Perihan Savaş ve Fikret Kuşkan, görüntü yönetmeni Feza Çaldıran ile yönetmen Darin J. Sallam'dan oluşan saygın bir ana jüri tarafından değerlendirildi.
Bu akşam saat 20.30'da COP31 Yeşil Alan'daki Kongre Salonu'nda gerçekleşecek yarışmada, dereceye giren sinemacılara çeşitli ödüller verecek. Dereceye giren finalistler sürdürülebilirlik vurgusu taşıyan, endüstriyel atıklar ve geri dönüştürülmüş malzemelerden özel olarak tasarlanan caretta caretta figürlü ödül heykelcikleri de verilecek.
COP31 Kısa Film Festivali kapsamında, Türk sinemasının usta sanatçıları da söyleşilere katılıyor. Ünlü sanatçı Hülya Koçyiğit, Berlin'de Altın Ayı kazanarak sinema tarihimizin ilk uluslararası başarısına imza atan başyapıtı Susuz Yaz ile COP31 İklim Temalı Kısa Film Yarışması'nın konuğu oluyor.
Koçyiğit, saat 17.30'da sinema yazarı Aslıhan Saraçoğlu moderatörlüğünde; su, doğa ve insan ilişkisini sanatçı perspektifiyle değerlendirecek.
Sanatçı ve yönetmen Uğur Yücel de saat 18.30'da senarist ve yapımcı Suat Köçer moderatörlüğünde; insan-doğa ilişkileri, değişen sinema seyirci algısı ve dijitalleşmenin etkileri üzerine gözlemlerini paylaşacak.
Filistinli yönetmen Darin J.Sallam da yönetmen Abdullah Harun İlhan moderatörlüğünde gerçekleşecek buluşmada, işgalin doğa ve canlılar üzerindeki ekolojik yıkımlarını ve Filistin direnişinin sinemadaki yansımalarını aktaracak.
COP31 Kısa Film Festivali kapsamında ayrıca mülkiyet, su hakkı ve kuraklık temalarını sinematik bir dille ele alan Metin Erksan imzalı Susuz Yaz filminin özel gösterimi yapılacak.
Film gösterimleri, Hülya Koçyiğit ve Uğur Yücel söyleşilerinin ardından saat 20.30'da ödül töreni düzenlenecek. Çok sayıda davetli ve sinemacıların katılacağı gecenin sunuculuğunu ise ünlü oyuncular Cem Davran ve Ekin Olcayto üstleniyor.

A Milli Kadın Basketbol Takımı, 2027 FIBA Avrupa Şampiyonası Elemeleri 2. tur I Grubu ikinci maçında İsrail'i 76-67 yendi.
Karşılaşmaya iyi başlayan ay-yıldızlılar, üst üste bulduğu 7 sayıyla 4. dakikaya 10-4 önde girdi. Üç sayı çizgisinin gerisini etkili kullanan Türkiye, ilk periyodu 22-10 üstün tamamladı.
Milliler, ikinci çeyrekte yakaladığı 8 sayılık seriyle rakibine kolay hücum etme şansı vermedi ve 13. dakikada İsrail'e mola aldırdı. Pota altını iyi kullanan ay-yıldızlı ekip, 15. dakikada Elif Bayram'ın basketiyle rakibiyle arasındaki farkı 13 sayıya çıkardı: 22-35. İsrail'in savunmadaki kötü oyununu Alperi Onar ve Meltem Yıldızhan ile iyi değerlendiren milli takım, soyunma odasına 47-29 önde gitti.
İkinci yarıya rahat başlayan Türkiye, 26. dakikada İsrail ile arasındaki farkı 20'ye yükseltti: 40-60. Çekişmeli geçen son bölümde İsrail 9 sayılık seri yakalasa da üçüncü periyot, millilerin 60-49 üstünlüğüyle sonuçlandı.
Son çeyrekte İsrail, boyalı alanı iyi kullanan taraf oldu ve 36. dakikada farkı tek sayıya indirdi: 55-64. Müsabakanın son saniyeleri büyük heyecana sahne oldu. İsrail, arka arkaya bulduğu 3 sayılık atışlarla farkı kapatmaya çalışırken Gökşen Fitik, başarılı serbest atışlarıyla farkın erimesine izin vermedi. Ay-yıldızlılar, karşılaşmadan 76-67 galip ayrıldı.
Türkiye'nin Letonya Büyükelçisi Ahmet Cemil Miroğlu ile Türkiye Basketbol Federasyonu Yönetim Kurulu üyeleri, mücadeleyi salonda takip etti.
Milliler, gruptaki 3. maçında 17 Kasım Salı günü TSİ 19.00'da Polonya'ya konuk olacak.
A Milli Kadın Basketbol Takımı'nda başantrenör Frederic Dusart ile milli basketbolcu Alperi Onar, Rimi Olympic Centre'da oynanan karşılaşmanın ardından AA muhabirine açıklamalarda bulundu.
İlk yarıda iyi bir oyun sergilediklerini kaydeden Fransız başantrenör, "İsrail'in vazgeçmeyen bir takım olduğunu ve savunmalarının bir problem olacağını biliyorduk. İlk yarı iyi iş çıkardık. İkinci yarıda ne oldu bilmiyorum. Sanırım biraz rahatladık ve geriye çekildik. Mental olarak oyunun dışına çıkmaya başladık. Kazanmak güzel ama özellikle ikinci yarıdaki oyunumuzla kazanmak benim için iyi bir şey değil. Polonya karşısında ikinci yarıdaki oyunumuz gibi oynamak yeterli olmayacaktır." diye konuştu.
Dusart, 17 Kasım Salı günü oynayacakları Polonya maçının zor olacağını belirterek, "Takımda Avrupa Ligi tecrübesi olan kaliteli oyuncular var. Polonya maçına odaklanmadan önce nasıl en iyi şekilde oynayabileceğimizin üzerine çalışmalıyız. Bugün 35 dakika boyunca iyi oynadık ancak bu Polonya karşısında yeterli olmayacaktır. Öncelikle hatalarımızı düzeltmeliyiz. Sonrasında Polonya maçı hakkında konuşabiliriz." ifadelerini kullandı.
Milli oyuncu Alperi Onar, eleme maçlarında her mücadeleyi kazanmanın önemli olduğunu vurguladı.
Frederic Dusart'ın yeni sistemine alışma aşamasında olduklarını anlatan Alperi, şunları söyledi:
"Kazanmak önemliydi. Yeni hocamızın yeni sistemine alışıyoruz ve ilk kamptan arka arkaya maçlar oynuyoruz. Fazla antrenman yapma fırsatımız olmuyor. Enerjimizle ilk yarıda orayı dengeledik ancak ikinci yarıda iniş ve çıkışlarımız oldu. Pencere maçlarında en önemli şey kazanmak. Eminim ki gelişerek ve büyüyerek devam edeceğiz."
Alperi, Polonya karşılaşmasında daha sert savunma yapmaları gerektiğini dile getirerek, "Hücumsal olarak yeni hocamıza alışmaya çalışıyoruz. Ama savunmada enerjimizi vermeliyiz ve daha istekli olmalıyız. Polonya iyi bir takım. Bu iki maçı ders olarak alacağız, bu maçları kazanmak önemliydi. Hatalarımızı düzeltmeye çalışacağız. Yarın Polonya'ya gideceğiz. Hazırlanmak için bir günümüz var. O yüzden olabildiğince hazır olup kazanmak için mücadelemizi vereceğiz." değerlendirmesinde bulundu.

Üstelik bütün bunları kimse sana söylemeden, kendi kendine yapıyor olabilirsin. İç sesin zaman zaman en acımasız eleştirmenin hâline geliyorsa bunun bazı davranışsal işaretleri vardır. Aşağıdaki 20 davranışı incele ve kendinde gördüklerini işaretle.
Eğer seçmek istediğin tüm şıkları seçtiysen. Sonucu görmek için yandaki butona tıkla!
Kendini sürekli yargılama eğilimin oldukça düşük görünüyor. Elbette sen de hata yapıyor, zaman zaman geçmişte söylediklerini düşünüyor veya kendini eleştiriyor olabilirsin. Ancak bu düşüncelerin günlük hayatını ele geçirmesine genellikle izin vermiyorsun. Bir şey yolunda gitmediğinde bunu kişisel bir başarısızlık olarak görmek yerine yaşanmış bir deneyim olarak değerlendirebiliyorsun. Kendine dair olumlu özellikleri fark etmekte ve başarılarını sahiplenmekte de daha rahat olabilirsin. Bu durum, kendine karşı her zaman kusursuz bir anlayış gösterdiğin anlamına gelmiyor. Bazı anlarda kendini gereğinden fazla sorguladığın veya başkalarının fikirlerinden etkilendiğin zamanlar olabilir. Fakat bu düşüncelerin içinde uzun süre kaybolmak yerine yoluna devam edebiliyorsun. Kendine hata yapma hakkı tanıman, duygusal açıdan daha esnek davranmana yardımcı olabilir. Yine de kendini eleştirmediğin her anı olumlu, eleştirdiğin her anı olumsuz olarak değerlendirmemelisin. Önemli olan, eleştirinin seni geliştirmesi ve kendine zarar veren bir iç konuşmaya dönüşmemesi. Kendine karşı anlayışlı olmayı sürdürürken gerektiğinde eksiklerini kabul etmek de güçlü yanlarından biri olabilir.
Kendini yargılama eğilimin bazı durumlarda belirginleşiyor. Özellikle hata yaptığında, birinden olumsuz geri bildirim aldığında veya beklentilerini karşılayamadığını düşündüğünde iç sesinin tonu değişebiliyor. O anlarda kendine karşı oldukça sert davranabilir, yaşanan bir olayı olduğundan daha büyük hâle getirebilirsin. Bazen çevrendeki insanlar yaşananları çoktan unutmuşken sen aynı konuşmayı veya davranışı zihninde yeniden canlandırıyor olabilirsin. Muhtemelen kendinden yüksek beklentilerin var. Bir işi iyi yapmakla yetinmeyip mümkün olan en iyi şekilde tamamlamaya çalışıyor olabilirsin. Ancak bu beklentiler karşılanmadığında başarılarını küçümsemek ve eksiklerine odaklanmak gibi bir eğilim geliştirebilirsin. Başkalarının düşüncelerini de fazlasıyla önemsemek, kendi kararlarını sorgulamana neden olabilir. Herkesin seni beğenmesini, onaylamasını veya doğru anlamasını beklemek yorucu bir döngü yaratabilir. Kendine yönelttiğin eleştirilerin her zaman gerçeği yansıtmadığını hatırlaman önemli. Bir hata yapmak seni başarısız, birini üzmek seni kötü bir insan, bir günü verimsiz geçirmek seni tembel yapmaz. Kendine yakın bir arkadaşına nasıl davranıyorsan öyle davranmayı deneyebilirsin. Çünkü senin de anlayışa, sabra ve ikinci bir şansa ihtiyacın var.
İç sesin günlük hayatında oldukça fazla yer kaplıyor olabilir. Yaptığın bir şeyin doğru olup olmadığını sık sık sorguluyor, geçmişte yaşanan olayları zihninde tekrar tekrar değerlendiriyor ve çoğu zaman kendine karşı başkalarından çok daha katı davranıyor olabilirsin. Birisi seni eleştirdiğinde yalnızca o davranışını değil, bütün kişiliğini sorgulamaya başlayabilirsin. Üstelik ortada somut bir eleştiri olmasa bile insanların seni nasıl değerlendirdiğine dair tahminler yürütüyor olabilirsin. Bu durum, kendini sürekli geliştirmeye çalışan ve sorumluluklarını önemseyen biri olmanla ilişkili olabilir. Ancak gelişmek için kendini sürekli suçlaman gerekmez. Hatta kendine yönelttiğin yoğun eleştiriler zaman zaman harekete geçmeni zorlaştırabilir. Bir işe başlamadan önce yeterince iyi yapamayacağını düşünmek, karar verirken defalarca fikir değiştirmek veya başarı elde ettiğinde bile rahatlayamamak bu döngünün parçaları olabilir. Kendine koyduğun standartlar o kadar yüksek olabilir ki hiçbir başarı sana yeterli gelmeyebilir. Burada üzerinde durman gereken şey, kendini eleştirmeyi tamamen bırakmak değil, eleştirinin dozunu ve dilini değiştirmek. Bir hata yaptığında kendine neden böyle yaptığını sorabilirsin ama kendini aşağılamak zorunda değilsin. Bir başkasının seni sevmesi için kusursuz olman gerekmediği gibi, kendine değer vermek için de her zaman başarılı olman gerekmiyor. Kendini yalnızca yaptıkların üzerinden değerlendirmemeyi öğrenmek, bu zihinsel yükü hafifletmenin önemli adımlarından biri olabilir.
Kendine yönelttiğin eleştiriler hayatının pek çok alanına yayılmış olabilir. Söylediğin bir cümleden aldığın bir karara, tamamladığın bir işten sosyal ilişkilerine kadar birçok konuda kendini sorguluyor olabilirsin. Üstelik çoğu zaman başkalarının sana yöneltmediği eleştirileri kendi içinde üretiyor olman mümkün. Birinin yüz ifadesini yanlış yorumlayabilir, kısa bir mesajı defalarca okuyabilir veya geçmişte yaşadığın bir olayı zihninde tekrar tekrar canlandırabilirsin. Sanki sürekli kendini değerlendiren görünmez bir jüri varmış gibi hissedebilirsin. Bu yoğun öz eleştiri, kendinden çok şey beklediğini ve hata yapmaya karşı tahammülünün düşük olabileceğini düşündürüyor. Başarılı olduğunda bile rahatlayamamak, başkalarının onayına ihtiyaç duymak, dinlenirken suçluluk hissetmek veya kendini başkalarıyla kıyaslamak seni zihinsel açıdan yorabilir. Zamanla kendi ihtiyaçlarını ikinci plana atabilir ve çevrendeki insanların beklentilerini karşılamaya çalışırken ne istediğini unutabilirsin. En zorlayıcı tarafı ise kendine ne kadar çabalarsan çabala yeterli olmadığını hissettirebilmesidir. Öncelikle kendinle kurduğun ilişkinin değişebileceğini bilmelisin. Her düşüncenin doğru olmadığını, her hatanın telafi edilebileceğini ve herkesin zaman zaman yanlış kararlar verebildiğini hatırlamak önemli. Kendini yargıladığın anlarda, aynı durumda sevdiğin birine ne söyleyeceğini düşünmek sana farklı bir bakış açısı kazandırabilir. Bu düşünceler yoğunlaşıyor, günlük yaşamını, ilişkilerini veya ruh hâlini belirgin biçimde etkiliyorsa bir ruh sağlığı uzmanından destek almak da faydalı olabilir. Unutma, kendine karşı nazik olmak bir zayıflık değil; kendinle kurduğun ilişkinin temel ihtiyaçlarından biri.
